title: Forces and Their Effects
seo_title: Primary 6 Science: Forces and Their Effects Worksheets (PSLE Practice with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 6: Interaction of forces (Forces and their effects)
standard_text: Recognise that a force is a push or a pull and that it can move a stationary object, speed up, slow down or stop a moving object, change the direction of motion and change the shape of an object. Measure forces in newtons with a spring balance (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on forces: pushes and pulls, effects of forces, measuring forces with a spring balance, balanced and unbalanced forces. PSLE practice with answers.
key_big: A force is a push or a pull.
key_sub: It can change speed, direction or shape.
body_html:
How to think about it

A force is a push or a pull. It is measured in newtons (N) with a spring balance.

A force can:

  • move a stationary object,
  • make a moving object speed up, slow down or stop,
  • change the direction of a moving object,
  • change the shape of an object.

Gravitational and magnetic forces can act without touching. When forces are balanced, a still object stays still.

Example

A pupil squeezes a ball of plasticine. What does the force do?

The plasticine is pressed

Its shape changes

Answer: It changes the shape.

Example

Siti pushes a box right with 30 N; Ravi pushes left with 20 N. Which way does it move?

The forces are unbalanced

30 N is bigger

Answer: To the right.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a still object has no forces on it. The forces are balanced.
  • Thinking a force is needed to keep a moving object going. Without friction it would keep moving.
  • Thinking forces can only make things move. They can also change shape or direction.
  • Measuring force in kilograms. Force is measured in newtons.

faq.q: Are there forces on an object that is not moving?
faq.a: Yes. The forces are balanced. For example, gravity pulls a book down and the table pushes it up.
